en: Points of Controversy,
Great Fifty-Section,
Tenth Chapter
The Discussion on the Moral Discipline of Intimation.
Is intimation moral discipline? Yes.
“Abstaining from taking life”?
One should not say so …pe… “Abstaining from taking what is not given”? One should not say so.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Abstaining from sexual misconduct”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
"Abstinence from false speech"?
One should not say so...
"Abstinence from fermented and distilled liquors, which are the basis for negligence"? One should not say so.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Paying homage is virtue;
rising to meet [a guest] is virtue; joining the palms in salutation is virtue; performing services with respect is virtue; offering a seat is virtue; offering a bed is virtue;
offering water for washing the feet is virtue; offering a footstool is virtue; bathing [the guest] is virtue.
Is back-massage virtue?
Yes. Is it the abstention from taking life? No.
It should not be said thus... [as before] ...
"Abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence"?
It should not be said thus... [as before].
Is it not to be said that “intimation is virtue”?
Yes, it is.
“Is it wrong conduct?
“One should not say so.
… [as before] … “In that case, then, intimation is virtue.”
The Discussion on the Threefold Nature of Intimation is finished.
